description: FIRST SKETCH-ON-A-MODEL-FACE GOLDEN (stage-1 topological naming): a boss-on-top built as a TWO-body-feature tree where the SECOND sketch sits on a PLANAR FACE OF THE FIRST BODY, not an origin/offset datum. Five features: (1) a 40x40 mm square on the XY origin datum; (2) extrude add 10 mm -> a 40x40x10 base box; (3) an ON_FACE datum whose plane is resolved from the base box's TOP face, named by a stage-1 SubshapeRef signature (normal +Z, area centroid (0,0,10), area 1600) matched against the recomputed body (docs/design/topological-naming.md 2b/4, datum-planes.md 7); (4) a 20x20 mm square on THAT datum (a FeatureRef to feature 3, the same mechanism an offset datum uses); (5) extrude add 10 mm -> a 20x20x10 boss fused onto the base top. Locks: the datum-from-face resolver (planar-face enumeration + signature match, exactly-one-or-error) + the deterministic derived sketch basis (origin at the face centroid, z_dir the outward normal, x_dir pinned from the normal) + the resolve_sketch_plane FeatureRef funnel carrying the on-face plane + the add boolean fusing boss to base, and -- via the parametrized round-trip gate -- STEP re-import of the fused stepped B-rep. The face reference resolves DETERMINISTICALLY across a rebuild: the in-process and fresh-interpreter determinism gates re-evaluate the whole tree (including the signature match against the rebuilt body) and require byte-identical GLB + identical metadata.
derivation: Expectations are HAND-DERIVED analytic values, not recorded harness output (geometry-gates skill: a golden recorded from buggy output enshrines the bug). Base sketch: an axis-aligned 40x40 square, corners (+/-20, +/-20) mm on the XY datum (normal +Z at world z=0); extrude add 10 mm up -> base box x,y in [-20,20], z in [0,10]. Its TOP face is planar, normal +Z, area centroid (0,0,10) mm, area 40*40 = 1600 mm^2 -- the exact stage-1 signature stored in feature 3's SubshapeRef.

On-face datum: the resolver enumerates the base box's planar faces (all 6 are planar), matches the stored signature (normal +Z, centroid (0,0,10), area 1600) against them, finds EXACTLY ONE (only the top face has normal +Z; the bottom is -Z, the sides +/-X/+/-Y), and derives its plane: origin at the centroid (0,0,10), z_dir the outward normal (0,0,1), and x_dir pinned deterministically from the normal to world +X (the world axis least aligned with +Z, ties broken X<Y<Z). offset_mm = 0, so the plane sits on the face.

Boss sketch: a 20x20 square, corners (+/-10, +/-10) in the datum's local frame; local (x,y) maps to world (x, y, 10) through the derived plane, so the boss footprint is x,y in [-10,10] at z=10. Extrude add 10 mm up +Z -> boss box x,y in [-10,10], z in [10,20], fused onto the base top (a coplanar interface at z=10, zero-volume overlap) -> one stepped solid.

volume = base + boss = 40*40*10 + 20*20*10 = 16000 + 4000 = 20000 mm^3 exactly (the boss and base share only the z=10 interface plane -> additive, no double count). Measured deviation vs analytic: exactly 0.0.

surface_area = bottom (40x40 = 1600) + 4 base walls (40x10 = 400 each = 1600) + shoulder (the base top annulus, 40x40 - 20x20 = 1600 - 400 = 1200) + 4 boss walls (20x10 = 200 each = 800) + boss top (20x20 = 400) = 1600 + 1600 + 1200 + 800 + 400 = 5600 mm^2. The base-top and boss-bottom interface faces are internal after the fuse+clean and contribute no external area. Measured deviation: 9.1e-13 mm^2 (one-ulp at the 5.6e3 scale).

centroid = (0, 0, 7.0) mm on the axis of symmetry: base slab (V=16000, z-centroid 5) and boss (V=4000, z-centroid 15) give z = (16000*5 + 4000*15)/20000 = 140000/20000 = 7.0; x,y = 0 by symmetry (GProp puts x,y at ulp scale ~5e-17, z within 2.7e-15 of 7.0).

bounding_box = [-20,-20,0]..[20,20,20]: the base spans +/-20 in x,y at z in [0,10] and the boss runs the full height up to z=20. Extrusion of a planar face is an exact prism, so the fused optimal AABB is EXACT (measured deviation 0.0 on all six bounds -- unlike the ThruSections loft golden, there is no AABB padding here).

topology: 11 faces (1 bottom cap + 4 base walls + 1 shoulder = the base top as ONE planar face with an inner square hole where the boss meets it + 4 boss walls + 1 boss top cap), 24 edges (4 bottom + 4 base verticals + 4 base-top outer + 4 boss-footprint inner + 4 boss verticals + 4 boss-top = 24), 1 closed shell. Cross-check by the generalized Euler-Poincare formula V - E + F = 2(S - G) + (L - F): with V=16 topological vertices, E=24, F=11, S=1 shell, G=0 genus, and L=12 loops (10 single-loop faces + the shoulder's 2 loops), 16 - 24 + 11 = 3 = 2*(1-0) + (12-11) = 2 + 1 = 3. Consistent.

mesh (linear 0.1 mm / angular 0.1 rad, faceted per-face normals, no vertex sharing across faces -- the box-golden convention): bottom cap 4 verts / 2 triangles; 4 base walls 4 verts / 2 triangles each = 16 / 8; shoulder (a square annulus, 4 outer + 4 inner corners) triangulates to 8 verts / 8 triangles (the picture-frame triangulation: each of the 4 frame sides is a quad -> 2 triangles); 4 boss walls 16 / 8; boss top cap 4 / 2. Totals = 4 + 16 + 8 + 16 + 4 = 48 vertices and 2 + 8 + 8 + 8 + 2 = 28 triangles.

GLB byte size is deliberately NOT pinned here: it is asserted deterministic (byte-identical) by the runner within one kernel version, but pinning the absolute size would break on every glTF-writer upgrade without geometric meaning.
tolerance_rationale: Measured first, then set (geometry-gates skill: never copy a bound blindly). This is a fused PLANAR B-rep (Solid.extrude prisms + a fuse+clean), so unlike the ThruSections loft golden there is NO AABB padding. Measured deviations vs the analytic values (2026-07-12, build123d 0.11.1 / OCCT 7.9, planegcs 0.8.0): volume exactly 0.0, bounding_box exactly 0.0 on all six bounds, centroid <= 2.7e-15 mm (x/y on the axis at ~5e-17; z within 2.7e-15 of 7.0), and surface_area 9.1e-13 mm^2 (a single ulp at the 5.6e3 scale -- the dominant term). Documented ceiling 1e-9 is ~1100x the observed worst case (9.1e-13), headroom for platform FP variation across OCCT builds and the STEP round-trip re-measure, while staying 5 orders of magnitude tighter than the standing kernel linear tolerance (1e-7 m -> 1e-4 mm at model scale). The solver contributes zero error by construction (both squares are shape-pinned, under-constrained in whole-sketch position -> planegcs returns the drawn positions bitwise; solved == input). Loosening this further requires a reviewed kernel-level justification recorded here and in docs/GEOMETRY-QA.md.
